answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a ferrous hardware-bound deposit before it may trade, so creating fake identities costs real capital instead of free keystrokes. The deposit is released only after a cooling period of honest service, and repeat offenders lose it entirely. Public reputation is then painted as a visible pigment: one stained record follows every identity, so a bad actor cannot hide behind a fresh haven account without paying the deposit again. Sybil scale becomes an economic decision, not a free trick.
